messages:
sara: heads-up — noticed weird KV residency growth on a customer workload with long contexts (~50k tokens). eviction rate goes into a spiral and memory keeps creeping despite free attempts. attaching short perf dump below. :eyes:

chris: can you paste the profiler snippet? nvlink s/w mix?

sara: here's the tail from the runtime trace:
```
[kvcache] slot_reuse_hits=3124 slot_evictions=48219 kv_residency=129MB->1.9GB
[kvcache] page_walks=11902 page_map_conflicts=487 page_map_retries=2431
[kvcache] last_evict_latency_ms=482 batch_kernel=optimized_tile_64x64
gpu_arch=H100+MI250X (peer via NVLink)
```

anita: that page_map_conflicts number is alarming. similar to the "mapper thrash" we saw in INF-2138 but different pattern. is batching kernel switching often?

sara: yes — kernel selection toggles between tile and scalar memcpy when sequence distribution spikes. suspect fallback path is leaving stale slot metadata around; eviction walk then re-maps repeatedly.

mike: reproducer? even short one?

sara: small repro attached to the ticket: run `./tools/repro_kv_residency.sh --mix h100,mi250 --ctx 40000 --burst 200` — it shows steady climb over ~5 mins. will link logs in jira.

infra-bot: Created issue INF-2456: "KV residency spiral + page-map churn on mixed NVLink topo" — assignee unassigned. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2456 :white_check_mark:

chris: quick hypothesis: race between page-table remap and evict completion callback on hybrid devices. if the kernel path for compact copy does not publish the final owner bit before the async eviction completes, we could race to re-allocate same slot. that would look like a leak even though physically pages are moved.

anita: good call. also check shadow-metadata update ordering — we had one fix where we moved the write to the completion callback and it silently masked a different race. maybe the completion wasn't firing for some scalar fallback path.

mike: i profiled with Nsight — saw a big gap: some kernels stuck in `page_map_update` waiting on host-side atomics while others spin in `evict_walk`. NVLink appears to reorder timings under contention. trace snippet: `host_lock_wait_us=1200` on MI250 side, but 0 on H100.

sara: posted raw traces and a small traceviz link: https://internal-redwood/trace/1745129930 (safe to view) — the interesting window is 00:03:12 -> 00:04:40.

chris: next steps: 1) add an assert in page_map that validates owner transitions (non-atomic double-check) 2) add extra logging in scalar fallback kernel completion path 3) attempt canary with single memory fence after copy completion on MI250 to see if churn stops.

anita: i'll take (1) and (2). sara — can you run the canary patch (fence) on the repro rig? should be quick.

sara: on it. running now — will post results in ~10m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued to test-hybrid-1 cluster (h100/mi250x) — tag: canary/kv-fence-2026-03-18. notify when done.

sara: quick update after 12 mins: eviction spiral reduced drastically, residency stabilized around 180MB. page_map_conflicts down to 12. still seeing a few stray retries but much better. logging attached to INF-2456.

mike: nice! that strongly implies ordering issue. we should still add a targeted unit test: force concurrent evict/map on mixed topo and assert no net residency growth.

chris: agreed — put test under runtime/kv/tests/concurrency_repro (small, deterministic). if green, we'll cherry-pick patch to stable and schedule a full regression run on 3x hybrid rigs.

anita: adding regression job to perf CI and marking INF-2456 as in-progress. i'll also audit other fallback kernels for missing publish fences.

sara: thanks all. summary in INF-2456 with logs, repro, and candidate patch. follow-ups: testcase + CI + backport. :thumbsup:
